SMTO-SCH-0028 — The Agent changed your task's wording when scheduling it

GUID: fcffae57-de75-4a82-8d87-8a1296ec131c
Slug: future-task-prompt-mismatch
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • You asked for a task to run later, but the Agent tried to save it with different instructions, leaving something out or adding something new. SMTO stopped it before anything was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Keep the conversation open. The Agent is told to save your task using your own words. SMTO makes sure the later run does exactly what you asked, not the Agent's rewording.
  2. Open Schedules, select Edit on the new schedule, and read the Instruction box to confirm it matches what you asked. This is the text the Agent will follow when the schedule runs.
  3. If you want different instructions, change them in the editor and save, or send a new message with the new wording. Changes you make yourself are kept as you wrote them.

What success looks like

  • The schedule on the Schedules page shows your instruction with nothing missing or added.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't turn off the Enforce temporal routing check to get past this; it could make the Agent act at the wrong time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Temporal routing rejected schedule.create because the scheduled prompt omits, replaces or adds instructions relative to the captured deferred user instruction.

What this means

  • After timing matches, deferred prompt validation finds omitted, replaced or added instruction text relative to the captured expected prompt. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • After timing matches, deferred prompt validation finds omitted, replaced or added instruction text relative to the captured expected prompt.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact expected_prompt with the proposed prompt, keeping timing in its dedicated fields.

How to fix it

  • After timing matched, _prompt_matches found canonical_task(prompt) equals neither the route's deferred_task nor its child_prompt. The model must copy expected_prompt from the correction exactly, keep the timing only in the schedule fields (not in the prompt text), and not add or drop work.
  • Preserve the captured deferred task prompt exactly. Keep its timing wrapper in schedule fields and do not add new work to the prompt.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The durable schedule preserves the intended deferred instruction without new work or missing requirements.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
